verdict: promote_as_best_balanced_access_branch; preserves 120/120 app behavior, keeps decoder geometry effectively unchanged, slightly improves measured stage82 NLL/BPB versus v424, and doubles answer-card retrieval top1 over v424 baseline. hypothesis: Amplify recursive semantic compression experiments by training a parameter ladder on stage429 answer-card retrieval, measuring verified answer-card access density across 1k/10k/100k/1m/10m presets instead of relying on unconstrained decoder generation.
verdict: strong_support_for_semantic_codec_training_signal; answer-card retrieval saturates by the 100k-1m range under explicit contrastive semantic-card supervision, while the prior 100m decoder-oriented branches remain far lower on the same probe. This does not make the tiny decoder generally smarter by itself, but it proves that compiled knowledge cards plus retrieval/probe supervision produce vastly higher verified semantic access per parameter than asking the unconstrained decoder to emit MDL JSON. Next step should transfer this access path back into the 100m production model via retrieval-augmented app orchestration or train a small semantic-access sidecar, while keeping v424/v430 decoder behavior protected.

hypothesis: Locate the parameter/training-token sweet spot by comparing 100-step and 400-step answer-card retrieval rungs using verified bits per training token and verified bits per parameter.

metrics.metric_definition: verified_bits = top1_correct_answer_card_retrievals * log2(unique_eval_answer_cards); estimated_training_tokens = completed_steps * batch_size * average train retrieval query+doc token count

verdict: 100-step runs are more token-efficient than 400-step runs on stage429; the 1m and 10m rungs reach about 96.8% top1 after only 100 steps, while 100k reaches 89.1% and has a much better parameter-efficiency profile. For this answer-card curriculum, the high-value search region is 100k-1m parameters with shorter runs and residual/hard-example replay, not blindly training larger models longer. The 10k rung remains the most parameter-dense lower-bound probe but is not saturated enough for reliable access.

hypothesis: Use the ladder evaluator as a recursive residual-compression loop: capture train-side retrieval failures from the 100k/100-step rung, oversample missed answer cards plus near-miss neighbors, and continue training to recover held-out semantic access with fewer parameters than the 1m rung.
verdict: positive; residual replay raises the 100k rung from 89.1% to 96.7% held-out answer-card top1, effectively matching the 1m/100-step rung while using about one-fifth the parameters. This is the clearest implementation of the recursive semantic residual idea so far: locate failures, train the residual, and remeasure verified bits/token. Next step is to make this loop automatic across rungs and stop when marginal verified bits per token falls below the next-size rung.

hypothesis: Map how a fixed 100k-scale model converts training tokens into verified answer-card access across short budgets, to distinguish token-efficiency optimum from raw accuracy saturation.
verdict: the 100k model learns the answer-card geometry rapidly; token efficiency peaks early around 50 steps in the measured grid, while raw top1 continues improving with diminishing returns. For practical capability, 100 steps plus residual replay is currently preferable to uniform continuation because it reaches 96.7% after targeted residual training, close to the 400-step raw top1 but with a clearer compression-control loop.

hypothesis: Move beyond plain answer-card retrieval by training semantic operations: direct facts, reverse lookup, false-claim rejection, default rules, exceptions, and two-hop composition, with both retrieval and decoder supervision.
verdict: semantic access generalizes beyond simple lookup: both 100k and 1m learn high retrieval accuracy on mixed fact/rule/exception/composition cards. However, free autoregressive answer generation remains the bottleneck even after switching to content-only targets. This suggests the next compression algorithm should treat the decoder as a constrained value selector or pointer/copy head over retrieved semantic cards, while the app supplies JSON/structure externally.

verdict: dense_wins_decisively_at_100k_on_stage429; full MLP expert replacement is not the right tiny-model compression move. hypothesis: Keep the dense tiny encoder MLP intact and add only a small routed residual adapter, testing whether expert specialization can improve verified bits/token or bits/parameter without destroying dense semantic geometry.
verdict: promising_density_not_raw_accuracy; routed residual adapters preserve most dense retrieval quality while using fewer parameters and producing better verified bits/token and bits/Mparam. Next test should run residual replay from this checkpoint and compare final held-out top1 against dense 100k residual replay.

hypothesis: Apply recursive residual replay to the routed residual-adapter MoE model to test whether expert residuals improve verified bits density after targeted failure replay.
verdict: positive_moe_density_result; routed residual adapter plus residual replay beats dense 100k raw top1 with fewer params and higher bits/Mparam, but still trails dense 100k residual replay in raw top1. Next compare on Stage430 semantic ops, where residual specialization may matter more than plain answer-card lookup.

hypothesis: Clean the semantic-ops curriculum by making reverse lookup set-valued, then compare dense vs routed residual-adapter MoE on semantically valid direct/reverse/rule/exception/composition targets.
verdict: clean_positive_moe_result; after fixing ambiguous reverse_lookup labels, routed residual adapters improve raw semantic retrieval top1 and bits/token over dense on the mixed operation curriculum, while dense remains slightly better on bits/Mparam because it has fewer parameters. This supports keeping MoE in the research sweep, but only as small routed residual capacity over a dense shared trunk.

hypothesis: Apply recursive residual replay to the cleaned Stage432 routed residual-adapter model and test whether a small set of remaining train misses transfers to held-out semantic operations.
verdict: positive_residual_compression; targeted replay from only 58 train misses lifted held-out cleaned semantic retrieval to 0.9890 top1. This supports the recursive compression loop on a semantically valid curriculum and makes routed residual adapters worth keeping in the sweep.

hypothesis: Check whether the routed residual adapter is learning operation-specialized experts or merely adding generic residual capacity.
verdict: weak_specialization; every semantic operation currently routes most tokens to expert 1. The Stage432 MoE gain is useful, but likely comes from extra routed residual capacity rather than clean operation-specialized experts. Next step should strengthen load balancing and add operation/domain-aware router probes before increasing expert count.

Keep the schedule flag for future experiments, but do not use high scheduled load balance as the default for Stage432.

verdict: operation_tokens_are_not_yet_a_compression_win; explicit textual operation prefixes preserve first-stage top1 and improve router balance compared with the original collapsed router, but they add substantial token overhead, do not produce clean operation-specialized experts, and replay underperforms the Stage432 low-balance replay checkpoint. hypothesis: Continue the recursive semantic compression loop from the Stage434 replay checkpoint by probing train misses, replaying only residual failures and near misses, and stopping when held-out verified retrieval plateaus.
verdict: positive_then_plateau; a second residual pass improves held-out semantic retrieval to 0.9953 top1, but a third smaller pass does not add another correct card. The residual loop is working, but generic replay is now saturated; remaining errors are specifically reverse_lookup_set confusions, so the next improvement should redesign set-valued inverse targets or add set-membership/pointer supervision.

hypothesis: Redesign the remaining ambiguous semantic targets by adding compact binding keys: first only for reverse lookup sets, then broadly for every operation, and compare target-specific keying against generic semantic keys plus residual replay.
verdict: new_best_and_stronger_target_design_evidence; narrow reverse-lookup binding keys plus residual replay beat the previous best, reaching 0.9969 top1. Broad semantic keys make direct facts perfect but spend too many tokens and fail to improve reverse sets. The compression lesson is precise: add structured tokens only where they remove real ambiguity, not as universal decoration.

hypothesis: Expand beyond direct/reverse retrieval into general semantic set use by adding set_count and set_member operations over compressed reverse lookup sets, then test whether residual replay transfers to the new derived operations.
verdict: positive_expansion_with_new_bottleneck; the tiny model handles a broader semantic curriculum extremely well, including perfect held-out direct facts, reverse sets, rules, exceptions, false claims, and two-hop composition. The remaining gap is no longer generic retrieval but derived set-count/member target design. Residual replay does not transfer, so the next upgrade should use more compact count/member targets or classifier-style supervision.

hypothesis: Fix the Stage445 set-count/member bottleneck by compressing the derived set-operation answer cards so the target contains only the operation key, domain/field/value binding, count or membership label, and omits the full entity list.
verdict: strong_target_compression_win; compacting derived set-operation targets fixes every held-out set_count and set_member miss while reducing token cost. The result supports the tiny-model training thesis: once the semantic operation is explicit, remove irrelevant target fields instead of replaying noisy cards or adding router pressure. Next curriculum should add harder derived set operations such as intersection, grouped counts, exception-aware counts, and multi-field filters.

hypothesis: After compact single-set count/member is solved, add two-constraint set_intersection_count and set_intersection_member operations to test whether the tiny routed residual model learns compositional set binding over compressed semantic cards.
verdict: positive_curriculum_expansion_with_residual_plateau; the model learns two-constraint intersection count and membership perfectly, so compact semantic cards scale to this harder derived operation. Remaining errors are direct same-entity wrong-field confusions. A narrow direct-fact key is not a net win because it steals capacity from rule defaults, and residual replay only shifts errors. Next target should factor direct answer cards into smaller value-selection cards or add a constrained value-selector head.

hypothesis: Test whether direct same-entity wrong-field confusions are fixed by compacting direct fact targets to only domain, entity, field, and answer, analogous to the Stage447 compact set-operation win.
verdict: negative; compact direct fact cards lower training/eval loss but do not improve direct held-out retrieval and introduce a reverse-set error. The direct fact residual is not solved by simply shortening target cards. The next candidate should factor value selection explicitly or add a constrained field/value selector head while preserving full cards for reverse-set geometry.

hypothesis: Preserve full direct fact cards for entity/reverse geometry while prefixing selected_field and selected_answer to make direct value binding more explicit.
verdict: neutral; selected_field/selected_answer lowers eval loss and avoids Stage451 reverse regression, but it does not improve verified held-out retrieval over Stage448. The residual direct-field errors likely require a separate value-selector/card-factorization objective rather than retrieval-card formatting alone.

Atomic improves at routed weight 8.0, and the full operation-sharded Stage764 aggregate under text_routed_multi_axis_compose_exact@8.0 reaches 1085.9898025078135 answer KBPP and 1066.4078684837573 exact KBPP. decision: Stage771 runs a balanced routed continuation probe with 128 rows per operation family. A 40-step continuation trains successfully and preserves the 16794-parameter shape, but routed and model-only eval scores are exactly unchanged. Short routed continuation preserves but does not improve this probe; the current KBPP gain is still carried by the factor scorer rather than a shifted neural retrieval geometry.

Routed and model-only eval scores remain exactly unchanged, so factor-table-only same-batch replay is preservation, not a KBPP amplifier.

decision: Stage773 mines residual train-split misses, attaches predicted wrong docs as hard negatives, and upweights miss rows. A 200-step hard-negative run improves model-only eval by one answer row and one exact row, but routed KBPP remains unchanged. Residual negatives are a better direction than plain replay, but current pressure is not enough to move the routed frontier.
label: stage773_residual_hardneg_probe

decision: Stage774 adds a procedure/schema branch to the routed factor mode. The balanced 1024-row probe improves from 0.23727969513471042/0.2333497201436422 to 0.39948048112970863/0.3969795879535743 answer/exact KBPP. The full Stage764 small shard improves from 17.68453018935334/17.6734548052876 to 18.69989281886388/18.69774919614148. Replacing only that small shard in the accepted Stage768 aggregate yields a canonical policy frontier of 1087.005165137324 answer KBPP and 1067.432162874611 exact KBPP. This is an accepted procedure-family routed-factor gain, not a new doubling rung.

decision: Stage775 remaps balanced residuals under text_routed_multi_axis_compose_procedure@8.0. The train residual target shrinks from Stage773's 383 routed miss rows to 69 answer misses and 75 exact misses. Eval has 37 answer misses and 43 exact misses. Remaining errors concentrate in schema, math identity, and composition/set-count, plus a small eval code API tail. Next build a targeted Stage776 residual-hardneg manifest instead of replaying the full balanced set.
label: stage775_procedure_routed_residual_map

decision: Stage776 builds the narrowed procedure-routed hard-negative dataset and trains a matched 16794-parameter 200-step continuation. The run lowers training loss but leaves top-1 unchanged: procedure-routed train/eval are exactly unchanged and model-only eval remains 44 answer-correct / 29 exact-correct. Stronger fixed hard negatives are not the next KBPP amplifier; the next change needs trainable procedure-family gates or factor-score scheduling.
label: stage776_procedure_routed_hardneg_training

decision: Stage777 trains the Stage776 residual-hardneg set with neural contrastive pressure only, then restores text_routed_multi_axis_compose_procedure@8.0 for scoring. Model-only eval improves by one row to 45/30 answer/exact correct, and procedure-routed eval improves by one row to 988/982, raising balanced answer/exact KBPP to 0.3998377515834421/0.39733685840730776. This accepts neural-first curriculum as a small positive training-side direction.
label: stage777_neural_hardneg_curriculum

decision: Stage778 starts from Stage777 and reintroduces the procedure factor at low training score weight 1.0 for 120 steps, then restores text_routed_multi_axis_compose_procedure@8.0 for scoring. It preserves Stage777's one-row gain but does not compound it: model-only eval remains 45/30 and procedure-routed eval remains 988/982 with answer/exact KBPP 0.3998377515834421/0.39733685840730776.
label: stage778_low_factor_reintro

decision: Stage779 isolates the single repaired row from Stage777/778. The only repaired eval row is schema unit stage653_d3548c0a96555b5b0335, split held_out_balanced_misc, expected tool_v30, worth 6 verified bits. There are no regressions, and train routed residuals remain unchanged at 69 answer misses and 75 exact misses.
label: stage779_stage778_residual_identity_map

decision: Stage780 repeats neural-only residual repair from the Stage778 checkpoint for 200 steps. It preserves but does not compound the Stage777 gain: model-only eval remains 45/30 answer/exact correct, and procedure-routed eval remains 988/982 with answer/exact KBPP 0.3998377515834421/0.39733685840730776. Repeating the same neural-only loop is saturated under the current objective.
label: stage780_second_neural_repair

decision: Stage781 runs a schema-only overfit diagnostic from Stage778 on the 50 Stage775 train schema exact misses with high neural loss weight. Model-only full balanced eval improves from 45/30 to 57/38 answer/exact rows, and procedure-routed answer improves from 988 to 992 with no answer regressions. Procedure-routed exact remains flat at 982 because two exact set-count repairs are offset by two exact set-count regressions. This confirms residual capacity under concentrated pressure but rejects another plain residual continuation as the next exact-KBPP amplifier; use a trainable schema/procedure factor-family gate with exact-margin protection.
label: stage781_schema_residual_overfit

decision: Stage782 starts from Stage781 and trains the narrowed 75-row procedure-routed exact residual set with composition/set-count exact rows weighted highest. Model-only eval improves from Stage781 57/38 to 69/49 answer/exact rows, and procedure-routed balanced eval improves from 992/982 to 993/983, answer/exact KBPP 0.40186228415459846/0.3976941288610413. This is a small positive exact-preserving balanced-probe gain; full-surface acceptance still requires shard scoring.
label: stage782_exact_protected_residual

decision: Stage783 freezes the Stage782 routed factor policy as a top-k/margin teacher and trains a mixed selector-dropped direct-answer plus route-proof distillation dataset. Model-only retrieval on the original balanced eval improves from Stage782 69/49 to 81/58 answer/exact rows while procedure-routed eval is preserved at 993/983. Direct generation remains unsolved: raw and prefixed direct-answer eval are both 0/256 pass. This is positive internalization for retrieval geometry but not yet open-ended answer emission.
label: stage783_routed_teacher_distillation

decision: Stage784 converts Stage783 to content-only decoder targets and trains from Stage783 with decoder loss emphasized. Direct generation still fails at 0/256 with zero mean recall, but retrieval internalization continues to improve: model-only original balanced eval reaches 89/65 and procedure-routed eval reaches 994/984. The next step should be decoder answer-only overfit or label/prefix masking repair before broad direct-answer training.
label: stage784_content_only_direct_answer

decision: Stage785's weak decoder-only overfit failed at 0/32, but Stage786's stronger matched decoder-only continuation reaches 28/32 direct pass and proves verified answer emission is learnable. The strong direct overfit damages retrieval, so it is diagnostic only; next use preservation-aware direct-answer training or a compact answer/value head.
label: stage785_786_direct_answer_overfit_diagnostic

decision: Stage787 trains only decoder, dec_norm, and lm_head parameters on the 32-row answer-only set. Direct answer generation improves to 12/32 while Stage784 model-only retrieval remains exactly 89/65 and procedure-routed retrieval remains exactly 994/984. This is the first preservation-compatible direct-emission recipe; next increase answer-emission capacity inside the frozen retrieval boundary.
label: stage787_decoder_lmhead_preserved_direct

decision: Stage788 continues the Stage787 decoder/lm-head-only path for 4000 more steps. It preserves Stage784 retrieval exactly, but direct answer generation regresses from Stage787 12/32 to 10/32 despite final loss falling to 0.2485. Lower decoder CE alone is rejected as the next direct-emission amplifier.
label: stage788_decoder_lmhead_longer_preserved_retrieval_direct_regressed

decision: Stage789 evaluates teacher-forced candidate answer likelihood ranking. It works for all-parameter Stage786 at 26/32 but fails for preserved Stage787/788 at 5/32 and 8/32. Candidate likelihood ranking is rejected as the preserved direct-answer mechanism; next build a supervised answer/value head or value-ranking contrastive loss over frozen retrieval features.
label: stage789_candidate_value_ranking

decision: Stage790 trains preservation-safe answer/value heads over frozen Stage784 features. A 279-parameter linear head solves the duplicated 32-row diagnostic at 32/32, but the broader 1024-row train/eval split rejects the simple class-head route: encoder-text linear gets 4/1024 eval, retrieval-query linear gets 2/1024 eval, and a 64-wide MLP memorizes train 1024/1024 while collapsing to 1/1024 eval. Next use query-candidate value ranking with same-collision negatives or route-conditioned value contrast over richer internal features.
label: stage790_frozen_answer_value_head

decision: Stage791 trains preservation-safe query-candidate value rankers over frozen Stage784 retrieval features. Unlike the plain answer-class head, the pairwise ranker improves the held-out 1024 direct-answer split: h128 raises same-collision eval answer top1 from base 243/1024 to 335/1024 and exact top1 from 232/1024 to 326/1024 with 8577 extra parameters. This is candidate-set ranking, not free-form generation; next integrate it as a route-conditioned value-ranking loss or adapter head and bridge it into direct answer emission.
label: stage791_frozen_query_candidate_value_ranker

decision: Stage792 adds explicit route/text binding features to the frozen query-candidate ranker. It reaches a 1023/1024 held-out candidate-ranking ceiling for both answer and exact top1, but this is not accepted as neural direct-answer KBPP because the access layer exposes domain/field/entity/token selector axes. The useful result is the internalization target: train route-feature heads or distillation so the model predicts these axes internally, then evaluate with explicit route features removed.
label: stage792_route_feature_candidate_ranker

decision: Stage793 applies a JEPA-style latent route-target auxiliary loss without feeding explicit route features at eval. The pair-ranker input remains frozen query/doc embeddings plus base dot score, while an auxiliary head predicts 11 route/text binding targets. This improves held-out answer/exact from Stage791 h128 335/326 to 343/334, a small positive gain far below the explicit-route Stage792 ceiling. Next use slot-specific route heads or feed predicted route features into the scorer.
label: stage793_jepa_route_target_ranker

decision: Stage794 feeds the predicted route latent back into the score head. The 1000-step feedback run improves held-out answer/exact to 354/346, beating Stage793 343/334 and Stage791 h128 335/326. This supports the JEPA route: predicted latent structure is useful as a scoring input. It remains far below the explicit-route Stage792 ceiling, so next use slot-specific route heads or a two-stage route predictor/value ranker.
label: stage794_predicted_route_feedback_ranker

decision: Stage795 pretrains the route latent predictor for 500 steps before predicted-route-feedback value ranking. It ties Stage794 on answer at 354/1024 and loses one exact row at 345/1024, so generic route pretraining is not the next amplifier. Keep Stage794 as the no-explicit-route frontier; next use slot-specific route heads or better-normalized route targets.
label: stage795_route_pretrain_feedback_ranker

decision: Stage796 narrows the predicted route target vector to binding9 and binary6 subsets under predicted-route feedback. Both regress relative to Stage794: binding9 reaches 351/341 answer/exact and binary6 reaches 341/329. The next amplifier is not simple target pruning; use architectural slot-specific heads or per-operation route heads.
label: stage796_normalized_route_target_feedback

decision: Stage797 remaps the Stage794 predicted-route-feedback ranker by operation. Stage794 remains the no-explicit-route internalization frontier at 354/346 answer/exact on the 1024-row held-out split. Residuals are not uniform: schema and code_api_semantics are strong, exception/counterfactual mostly track the base, while atomic_fact, relation, math_identity, and composition remain weak. The next amplifier should be per-operation or slot-specific route/value heads, not generic route-vector pruning or pretraining.
label: stage797_predicted_route_feedback_residual_breakdown

decision: Stages798-800 test operation conditioning for the JEPA-style predicted-route-feedback candidate ranker. Naive per-operation heads are rejected: Stage798 raises parameters to 80056 and regresses held-out answer/exact to 341/334. Shared operation one-hot features are positive: Stage799 reaches 362/355, and the longer Stage800 reaches 375/367 with 11031 ranker parameters. Stage800 becomes the current no-explicit-route candidate-ranking frontier, but atomic_fact regresses to 4/128, so the next amplifier should target atomic field/entity binding specifically rather than add more generic operation context.
label: stage798_800_operation_conditioning

decision: Stages801-802 test whether Stage800's atomic_fact regression is caused by loss allocation. Atomic loss weight 4.0 is mildly positive, reaching 377/369 answer/exact. Atomic loss weight 8.0 is stronger: Stage802 reaches 386/377 with the same 11031-ranker-parameter shared operation-feature scorer, recovering atomic_fact to 10/128 and creating the new no-explicit-route candidate-ranking frontier. This confirms operation-aware weighting helps, but atomic remains low; the next amplifier should add atomic field/entity slot binding rather than only increase weight again.
label: stage801_802_atomic_weighted_operation_feature

decision: Stages803-804 sweep route-target loss on top of Stage802's atomic-weighted operation-feature scorer. Raising route-target loss from 0.1 to 0.2 gives a small new frontier at 387/379 answer/exact, mainly through code_api_semantics, composition, and relation, while atomic slips from 10/128 to 9/128. Raising route-target loss to 0.3 regresses to 384/376. Decision: route supervision helps globally up to 0.2 but does not solve atomic; the next algorithmic step should add atomic field/entity slot binding rather than continue route-weight sweeps.
label: stage803_804_route_weight_atomic_weight

decision: Stage805 adds an atomic-only field/entity/token slot auxiliary loss on top of the Stage803 atomic-weighted operation-feature predicted-route-feedback scorer. It regresses held-out answer/exact from Stage803's 387/379 to 383/373, while atomic_fact stays at 9/128. Schema improves to 122/128, but relation, composition, code, and exact recovery lose enough rows that the shared atomic slot SmoothL1 objective is rejected. The next atomic amplifier should use a decomposed atomic field/entity contrastive target or atomic-specific predicted subscore, not another shared route-slot loss.
label: stage805_atomic_slot_loss_probe

decision: Stage806 adds a separate atomic binary slot head for field match, entity overlap, and gsel-field match, feeds its predicted logits back into the scorer, and trains it only on atomic_fact rows. This regresses held-out answer/exact from Stage803's 387/379 to 371/363, and atomic_fact falls from 9/128 to 7/128. The extra predicted atomic channel is rejected. The next atomic amplifier should use explicit atomic candidate partitioning, mined entity-field contrastive pairs, or a two-stage atomic scorer instead of another auxiliary head.
label: stage806_atomic_binary_feedback_probe

decision: Stages807-808 add a training-only atomic hard-negative margin against candidates sharing field, entity, or gsel-field with the query. Weight 0.25 reaches 385/377 answer/exact and weight 0.1 reaches 386/378, both below Stage803's 387/379. Atomic stays fixed at 9/128. The branch improves MRR but not top-1 KBPP, so the next atomic amplifier should use explicit candidate partitioning or a two-stage atomic reranker over mined entity-field partitions.
label: stage807_808_atomic_hardneg_margin

decision: Stage809 trains an atomic-only predicted-route-feedback ranker using the same frozen query/doc embeddings and no explicit route features at eval. It fails as a two-stage atomic specialist: held-out atomic answer/exact is 5/128, below Stage803's 9/128 and below the frozen base 7/128. Interpolating Stage803 with the atomic specialist also fails to improve top-1. The next atomic route needs a cleaner candidate partition or a representation change that exposes entity-field binding before scoring.
label: stage809_atomic_only_specialist

decision: Stage810 is a parser-based atomic candidate-partition ceiling diagnostic, not accepted model-only KBPP. It shows the atomic bottleneck is candidate partitioning: Stage803 scores only 9/128 atomic rows unpartitioned, field-only partitioning raises this to 39/128, entity-only to 60/128, and field+entity partitioning reaches 128/128 with singleton partitions. This explains why added heads, margins, and an atomic-only reranker failed. The next model-side target is to train/internalize atomic field+entity partition prediction.
label: stage810_atomic_candidate_partition

decision: Stage811 trains the shared Stage803 scorer with an additional atomic field+entity partition BCE loss directly on the candidate scores. This is rejected: held-out answer/exact falls to 370/362, and atomic falls to 7/128. The Stage810 partition teacher is correct, but pushing the partition objective into the shared score head damages the scorer and does not internalize atomic binding. Next use a separate partition module or representation-level field/entity binding objective.
label: stage811_atomic_partition_score_loss

decision: Stages812-813 train a separate atomic field+entity partition predictor from frozen pair features, using parser partition labels only during training. Stage812 is a small positive: predicted top-8 partition plus Stage803 scoring raises held-out atomic from 9/128 to 11/128, implying a full 1024-row hybrid of 389/381 answer/exact versus Stage803's 387/379. Stage813, a larger full-batch predictor, fails to improve. Next improve the partition representation with entity/field-aware token features, trainable binding embeddings, or base-model representation training.
label: stage812_813_atomic_partition_predictor

decision: Stage814 adds raw text-derived lexical binding features to the separate atomic partition predictor. Parser field+entity labels are used only for training; eval uses lexical overlap/binding features, not route labels. This reaches 128/128 held-out atomic top-1 with top-1 predicted partition, implying a full-split hybrid of 506/498 answer/exact if combined with Stage803 non-atomic rows. This is not accepted pure model-only KBPP because the lexical feature path is external, but it decisively identifies the missing representation: exact entity/field token binding.
label: stage814_atomic_lexical_partition_predictor

decision: Stage815 replaces Stage814's hand lexical features with a trainable hashed-token binding channel. Parser field+entity labels are training-only; eval uses raw token hashes and learned hash embeddings, not parser route labels. This reaches 128/128 held-out atomic top-1 with top-1 predicted partition, matching the Stage814 lexical ceiling and implying a full-split hybrid of 506/498 answer/exact with Stage803 non-atomic rows. This is the strongest architecture diagnostic so far: exact entity/field binding can be represented compactly by a learned hash-binding path.
label: stage815_atomic_hash_binding_partition_predictor

decision: Stage816 maps parser-derived partition ceilings by operation using Stage803 scoring inside the partition. This is a teacher diagnostic only. After atomic, the largest recoverable partition gains are relation via entity partitioning, composition via entity partitioning, and counterfactual via field+entity partitioning. Math identity does not improve under these partitions, so it needs a value/procedure-specific route. Combining each operation's best parser partition implies roughly 744/736 answer/exact over the 1024 split, versus Stage803's 387/379 and Stage815's atomic-only diagnostic hybrid 506/498.
label: stage816_operation_partition_ceiling

decision: Stage817 extends the Stage815 learned hash-token binding channel from atomic rows to atomic, relation, composition, counterfactual, and exception rows. Parser-derived binding labels are training-only; eval uses raw query/candidate token hashes, learned hash embeddings, an operation embedding, and Stage803 scoring after selection. Top-1 reaches an implied full 1024-row candidate-ranking diagnostic of 839/838 answer/exact, far above Stage803's 387/379, Stage815's atomic-only 506/498 diagnostic, and the Stage816 fixed parser-partition ceiling of 744/736. Because the learned hash-binding channel is selecting query-candidate bindings directly, this is an architecture diagnostic frontier, not yet proof of direct/open-ended model intelligence. Next audit held-out token aliases/hash buckets/paraphrases and integrate the selector as a native value/binding head.
label: stage817_multiop_hash_binding_selector

decision: Stage818 audits the Stage817 target rows with deterministic token-overlap baselines. Simple all-token overlap solves the 640 target rows at 640/640 answer/exact, while field+entity overlap reaches 446/441 and removing field/entity drops to 175/161. This reclassifies Stage817: the hash-binding selector is a useful architecture diagnostic, but the current surface is token-isomorphic and cannot count as accepted generalized internal KBPP. Next build a hardened Stage819 split with latent-equivalent but surface-different query/doc bindings, held-out aliases, and paraphrased operations before wrapping the selector around 100M training.
label: stage818_token_binding_shortcut_audit

decision: Stage819 v1 builds a hardened binding surface by replacing target-operation query and document entity/field tokens with side-specific aliases. The overlap audit drops all-token overlap from Stage818's 640/640 to 166/640 answer and 155/640 exact, and field+entity overlap drops to 40/640 and 23/640. Atomic, relation, composition, and exception are mostly unsolved by overlap, but counterfactual remains shortcut-prone at 128/128 answer because claim/status surface tokens still overlap. Next harden counterfactual claim/status text in Stage820 before retraining the learned selector.
label: stage819_hardened_binding_surface

decision: Stage820 fixes the Stage819 counterfactual shortcut by side-aliasing wrong claimed values while preserving answer= values for evaluation. Deterministic all-token overlap drops from Stage818's 640/640 to 40/640 answer and 39/640 exact on the target operations. Counterfactual specifically drops from Stage819's 128/128 answer shortcut to 2/128. This is the first hardened acceptance surface for retraining the learned binding selector: exact token overlap, field/entity overlap, and claimed-value overlap are now too weak to solve the benchmark.
label: stage820_hardened_counterfactual_surface

decision: Stage821 trains a learned hash-binding selector on the Stage820 hardened surface where exact query/doc token overlap no longer solves the task. The selector beats the deterministic overlap baseline, reaching 92/640 answer and 75/640 exact versus 40/39. However, train reaches 614/640 answer/exact, so the current hash-bag selector is memorizing train alias bridges much more than it generalizes to held-out aliases. As an implied full 1024-row hybrid with unchanged Stage803 non-target rows, this is only about 322/304 answer/exact, below Stage803's 387/379. Decision: positive proof that learned binding can recover some non-identical alias bridges, but not enough for 100M wrapping. Next use explicit latent-pair supervision, shared suffix/pair-code features, or contrastive qalias-dalias bridge training with held-out alias families.
label: stage821_hash_binding_selector_hardened

decision: Stage822 adds explicit contrastive bridge supervision for side-specific aliases on top of the Stage821 hardened hash-binding selector. This improves held-out hardened target rows from Stage821's 92/75 answer/exact to 132/112, versus the deterministic overlap baseline of 40/39. The gain is especially visible in counterfactual, exception, and composition. However, train remains near-solved at 615/615, and the implied full 1024-row hybrid is only 362/341 after adding unchanged Stage803 non-target rows, still below Stage803's 387/379. Decision: explicit alias-bridge supervision is the right next lever, but the current bag selector still overfits and needs stronger generalization pressure: bridge-weight sweep, held-out alias-family splits, and integration with Stage803 frozen embedding scores.
label: stage822_bridge_supervised_hash_binding_selector

decision: Stage823 adds relation:4.0 row weighting on top of the Stage822 bridge-supervised hardened selector. This is rejected. Held-out target answer/exact falls from Stage822's 132/112 to 100/81, and relation itself falls from 4/128 to 3/128. The weighting also damages composition, counterfactual, and exception. Relation is therefore not an exposure-allocation issue in the current hash-bag selector; it needs a relation-specific representation, pair-code bridge, or score fusion with Stage803 frozen embeddings.
label: stage823_relation_weighted_bridge_selector

decision: Stage824 fuses the Stage822 bridge-supervised hardened selector with frozen Stage784 query/doc embedding dot scores. This is not literal Stage803 trained-ranker fusion because no Stage803 ranker checkpoint is present, but it tests the intended score-composition route. Fusion is strongly positive: target rows improve from Stage822's 132/112 to 223/211 answer/exact at alpha 0.5. With unchanged Stage803 non-target rows, the implied full 1024-row hybrid is 453/440, beating Stage803's 387/379. Decision: score composition is the right route. Next make the fusion trainable and recover per-operation detail, then add relation-specific pair-code features because relation remains the main unknown under the aggregate fusion.
label: stage824_frozen_base_fused_bridge_selector

decision: Stage825 makes the Stage824 fusion calibration honest by selecting the fusion alpha on train, then reporting eval at that train-selected alpha. Train selects alpha 0.25. Eval at alpha 0.25 reaches 218/204 answer/exact on the hardened target rows. This is slightly below the eval-picked alpha 0.5 result of 223/211, but still strongly above Stage822 selector-only 132/112 and the deterministic overlap baseline 40/39. With unchanged Stage803 non-target rows, the train-calibrated implied full split is 448/433, beating Stage803's 387/379. Decision: calibrated score fusion is accepted as the new hardened candidate-ranking frontier. Remaining work is per-operation route improvement, especially relation and composition exactness, plus held-out alias-family validation.
label: stage825_train_calibrated_fusion

decision: Stage826 validates Stage825 on a stricter held-out alias-family surface: train and eval use different alias salts, so qent/dent, qslot/dslot, and qclaim/dclaim identifiers differ across splits. The current bridge selector/fusion does not generalize. Train-calibrated fusion drops from Stage825's 218/204 to 62/46, and even eval-picked fusion reaches only 76/60. Selector-only is 43/27. This fails the acceptance gate and shows Stage825 still depends on train/eval alias-family reuse. The next route needs compositional alias bridges, such as shared latent pair-code features or side-invariant alias decomposition, before any 100M wrapping.
label: stage826_heldout_alias_family_validation

decision: Stage827 adds side-specific latent pair-code tokens to the stricter held-out alias-family surface: query sees qpair_* and docs see dpair_* with stable suffixes across train/eval alias salts. This does not solve held-out alias generalization. Selector-only falls to 26/640 answer and 13/640 exact, while train reaches 640/640 and exposes a stronger overfit than Stage826. Fusion can be made to look better only by selecting alpha on eval: alpha 2.0 reaches 87/76, slightly above Stage826's eval-picked 76/60. The honest train-calibrated alpha is -0.25 and eval collapses to 23/11, below Stage826's 62/46. Decision: reject as an accepted route. Pair-code tokens make train too easy and break calibration; the next route should use a validation split or pair-code dropout/regularization, and more importantly learn side-invariant alias bridges without train-family memorization.
label: stage827_pair_code_heldout_alias_validation

decision: Stages828-829 test whether Stage827's pair-code fusion failure can be rescued by choosing the fusion alpha on held-out train calibration rows instead of optimized train rows. Stage828 uses a tail 20% calibration split and selects alpha 1.0, improving eval-at-selected-alpha to 75/63 versus Stage827's 23/11 and Stage826's 62/46. However, the tail calibration split is operation-skewed. Stage829 fixes that with stratified 20% calibration, but same-alias-family calibration still overfits: it selects alpha 0.25 and eval falls to 45/31. Eval-picked alpha 2.0 reaches 100/87, but that is not an acceptance metric. Decision: reject pair-code calibrated fusion as a robust route. The stable pair-code channel produces eval-picked upside but no reliable calibration under held-out alias-family validation. label: stage828_829_pair_code_calibration

Next improve the underlying bridge scorer, especially atomic/relation/counterfactual, while keeping external alias-salt calibration.

decision: Stages831-833 improve the external alias-salt calibration branch by changing the bridge scorer, then testing whether a wider fusion alpha range exposes additional calibrated accuracy. Stage831 upweights atomic_fact:3.0, relation:4.0, and counterfactual_false_claim:3.0; external calibration selects alpha 2.0 and eval reaches 129/640 answer and 114/640 exact, improving Stage830's 115/101. Decision: Stage832 is the current external-calibrated bridge-scorer frontier, with implied full split 362/346 after adding unchanged Stage803 non-target rows. This is progress, but still below Stage803's 387/379; next work should improve the representation or add operation-specific bridge heads rather than further scalar row weighting.
label: stage831_833_external_alias_scorer_weight

decision: Stage834 adds operation-specific scorer heads to the external alias-salt bridge selector, keeping the Stage832 scalar row weights and wide fusion alpha range. This is rejected. External calibration selects alpha 2.0 and eval reaches only 104/640 answer and 88/640 exact. Even eval-best alpha 6.0 reaches only 120/102, below Stage832's calibrated 132/117. The operation-specific heads increase selector parameters from 50177 to 119813 but do not improve held-out transfer; they appear to fragment the small calibrated surface and hurt exception/composition aggregate gains. Decision: keep Stage832 as the external-calibrated scorer frontier. Next representation work should share more structure, such as typed bridge feature channels or low-rank per-operation adapters, rather than fully separate scorer heads.
label: stage834_operation_specific_scorer

decision: Stages835-837 test shared low-rank per-operation adapters after full operation-specific heads failed in Stage834. Stage835 rank-8 is a real calibrated gain: external calibration selects alpha 8.0 and eval reaches 136/640 answer and 120/640 exact, improving Stage832's calibrated 132/117 with only 60897 selector parameters. Stage836 rank-16 has a higher eval-best diagnostic at 146/131, but external calibration selects alpha 3.0 and eval-at-selected-alpha is only 117/105, so it is not accepted. Stage837 rank-32 also regresses under calibration to 117/105, with eval-best 124/108. Decision: Stage835 rank-8 is the current external-calibrated bridge-scorer frontier, implied full split 366/349 after adding unchanged Stage803 non-target rows. This is still below Stage803 387/379. Next work should fix calibration/alpha robustness for higher-capacity adapters or add typed bridge channels; do not simply increase adapter rank.
label: stage835_837_lowrank_adapter

Stage838 combines typed bags with rank-8 low-rank adapters and improves calibrated eval to 138/640 answer and 125/640 exact, above Stage835's 136/120. Stage839 combines typed bags with rank-16 adapters and becomes the new frontier: external calibration selects alpha 2.0 and eval reaches 144/640 answer and 129/640 exact, with eval-best 146/132. Stage840 rank-32 regresses badly under calibration to 82/65 despite eval-best 128/111, so higher rank is not accepted. Decision: typed bridge channels plus rank-16 adapters are the current external-calibrated bridge frontier, implied full split 374/358 after adding unchanged Stage803 non-target rows. This is still below Stage803 387/379 by 13 answer rows and 21 exact rows; the remaining bottleneck is composition exactness and relation/atomic coverage, not calibration plumbing.
label: stage838_840_typed_bridge_channel

decision: Stage839 remains the accepted external-calibrated held-out-alias bridge frontier at 144/129 target rows, implied full 374/358. The next step is not another global scorer tweak; it is calibration-robust residual routing, likely operation- or family-specific alpha/gate selection using the external calibration split.
label: stage841_842_typed_residual_bridge

decision: Operation-specific alpha calibration is useful diagnostically but is not yet an accepted KBPP gain. The branch shows scorer headroom up to 160/145 under eval-oracle operation alphas, but external calibration rows do not reliably select those gates.
label: stage843_846_operation_calibration_gate

decision: Learned score-feature fusion gates do not solve the held-out alias calibration mismatch. The high-capacity gate overfits calibration and collapses on eval. A small regularized gate transfers better but still reaches only 109/95, below Stage846 global alpha 114/100, Stage846 operation alpha 117/101, and the accepted Stage839 frontier 144/129. The calibration branch is now closed for this scorer family.
label: stage847_848_score_feature_gate

A metadata teacher partition plus frozen base scoring reaches 479/465 target rows, versus Stage839 accepted 144/129 and Stage848 gate 109/95. Atomic and counterfactual are solved by entity+slot partitions. Relation and exception improve strongly with entity partitions. Composition improves with entity partitioning but remains the largest residual at 76/62, so proof-aware composition needs a better internal partition/scorer after entity narrowing.
label: stage849_hardened_partition_ceiling

decision: Stage850 trains a token-only hash-bag partition predictor to imitate the Stage849 metadata teacher policy, then evaluates by using predicted partitions only and frozen Stage784 base scores inside those partitions. It overfits the train alias bridge: train at the selected threshold reaches 412/640 answer and 400/640 exact, but held-out alias eval reaches only 96/640 answer and 76/640 exact. This is below the accepted Stage839 hardened bridge frontier of 144/129 and far below the Stage849 metadata partition ceiling of 479/465. The result rejects naive token-bag partition internalization. The next route should predict typed latent slots directly: operation, entity binding, slot/field binding, relation/proof role, and composition support, with alias-family dropout and proof-aware second-stage composition scoring.
label: stage850_token_partition_predictor

decision: Stage851 adds typed entity and slot partition heads to the Stage850 token predictor, with training-only same-collision candidate sampling capped at 64 candidates and full held-out eval. It is a positive diagnostic: train-selected eval improves from Stage850 96/76 to 128/109, and eval-best reaches 135/117. However, it remains below the accepted Stage839 hardened held-out-alias frontier of 144/129 and far below the Stage849 metadata teacher ceiling of 479/465, so it is not accepted as a new internalization frontier. The typed-slot decomposition is directionally right, but it needs stronger side-invariant bridge supervision and relation/composition proof heads.
label: stage851_typed_slot_partition_predictor

decision: Stage852 keeps the Stage851 typed entity/slot partition heads but normalizes q-side and d-side bridge prefixes before hashing: qent/dent -> ent, qslot/dslot -> slot, qclaim/dclaim -> claim, and qpair/dpair -> pair. This is a major accepted gain. Train-selected threshold 0.2 reaches 232/640 answer and 214/640 exact on held-out alias eval, beating Stage839's accepted 144/129 and Stage851's 128/109. Eval-best threshold 0.7 reaches 237/220. The implied full 1024-row split is 462/443 after adding unchanged non-target rows, above the prior full Stage803 frontier of 387/379. This proves the partition bottleneck was largely side-specific alias mismatch: typed heads need side-invariant bridge tokens. Remaining gap to the Stage849 teacher ceiling is mostly relation/composition proof quality and atomic/counterfactual partition precision.
label: stage852_side_invariant_typed_partition_predictor

decision: Stage853 reruns the Stage852 side-invariant typed partition predictor but selects the threshold on the external alias-salt calibration split instead of saturated train. Calibration selects threshold 0.7, which also matches eval-best. Held-out eval reaches 237/640 answer and 220/640 exact, improving Stage852 train-selected 232/214 and establishing the calibrated accepted frontier. The implied full 1024-row split is 467/449 after adding unchanged non-target rows, above Stage803's 387/379. The calibration split is now useful again once q/d aliases are normalized; next work should reduce partition size and close relation/composition proof gaps.
label: stage853_calibrated_side_invariant_typed_partition_predictor

decision: Stage854 tests whether the Stage853 side-invariant typed partition predictor can be improved without retraining by selecting thresholds per operation on the external calibration split. It is rejected as an accepted frontier: calibration-selected per-operation thresholds reach 233/640 answer and 216/640 exact on eval, below Stage853 global calibrated 237/220. Eval-oracle per-operation thresholds would reach 254/236, so threshold headroom exists, but the calibration split does not select it reliably per operation. Next work should change representation or add operation/proof heads rather than adding another threshold table.
label: stage854_per_operation_threshold_diagnostic

decision: Stage855 adds a role/proof head to the Stage853 side-invariant typed partition predictor and uses entity x role for relation/composition rows. It is rejected as a frontier. Calibration selects threshold 0.9 and eval reaches only 204/640 answer and 186/640 exact; even eval-best threshold 0.2 reaches only 221/202, below Stage853's calibrated 237/220. The role head sharply reduces mean partition size to 1.08125 at the selected threshold, but it over-prunes held-out positives, especially composition and relation. The finding is useful: role/proof binding should be a soft reranking feature or second-stage scorer, not a multiplicative hard partition gate.
label: stage855_role_head_partition_predictor

decision: Stage856 changes Stage855's hard role/proof gate into a soft role mix for relation/composition: entity * ((1-alpha) + alpha*role), with alpha=0.25. It is still rejected. Calibration selects threshold 0.9 and eval reaches only 203/640 answer and 185/640 exact; eval-best threshold 0.2 reaches 228/209, below Stage853's 237/220. The role-head training strongly improves train partitions but does not transfer across held-out aliases. The next role/proof route should not mix role scores into the first-stage partition probability; it should train a separate second-stage reranker inside Stage853 partitions or distill proof roles after the side-invariant partition is fixed.
label: stage856_soft_role_partition_predictor

decision: Stage857 keeps first-stage relation/composition partitioning at entity-only behavior with role_mix_alpha=0.0, then adds role/proof probability as a second-stage rerank feature with beta=0.25. It is rejected. Calibration selects threshold 0.9 and eval reaches only 200/640 answer and 182/640 exact; eval-best reaches 225/206, below Stage853's 237/220. The likely issue is that training the role head still shares and perturbs the partition embeddings. The next rerank route should freeze or detach the Stage853 partition predictor and train a separate role/proof reranker inside its selected partitions.
label: stage857_role_rerank_partition_predictor

decision: Stage858 detaches role-loss gradients from the shared partition embeddings while using role probability as a second-stage rerank feature with beta=0.25. It is rejected. Calibration selects threshold 0.9 and eval reaches only 197/640 answer and 180/640 exact; eval-best is 228/210, still below Stage853's 237/220. Detaching preserves the Stage853-like train partitioner, but the calibration split over-selects a tight threshold and the role reranker does not transfer. The current role/proof branch should close until a truly separate reranker dataset/validation protocol is built inside Stage853-selected partitions.
label: stage858_detached_role_rerank

decision: The last 100 stages moved from factor-assisted 256 KBPP closure to a calibrated model-side hardened held-out-alias frontier above the Stage803 full candidate-ranking reference. The correct next branch is frozen Stage853 partition materialization plus a separate reranker; in-trainer role/proof variants should stop.
label: stage759_858_last100_progress_analysis

Stage860 trains a separate 209-parameter reranker inside frozen Stage859 partitions using base score, partition probability, rank, partition size, and operation. Reject score/probability-only reranking; next reranker needs candidate content, frozen embeddings, role/proof/value features, or direct answer evidence.

Stage861 adds frozen query/doc embedding-pair features inside frozen Stage859 partitions. Raw eval improves from 237/220 to 239/222 target rows, implied full 469/451. Stages862-864 test h16, h64, and linear frozen embedding rerankers. Raw eval reaches 238/221, 238/221, and 232/215 respectively, all below Stage861 raw 239/222. The robust signal is operation selectivity, not more or less capacity.

Stage865 diagnoses calibration-margin operation gating. A conservative gate blocks unstable relation and exposes diagnostic headroom up to 248/231 target rows, but because it is posthoc it is not treated as the accepted frontier.

Raw reranker is rejected at 234/217, but the fixed gate selects composition and exception and improves eval to 242/225 target rows, implied full 472/454. Stage877 combines accepted operation policies while preserving frozen Stage859 partitions: composition scalar fusion, Stage866 exception embedding component, and base ordering for atomic/counterfactual/relation. Stage907 materializes broad bridge curriculum targets from frozen Stage859 partitions across atomic_fact, relation, composition, counterfactual_false_claim, and exception. Stage915 trains proof_edge_match as a fifth frozen-hidden auxiliary target using Stage913 labels. Calibration reaches 267/262 but eval falls to 201/184, below Stage859 base 237/220. Reject naive joint multi-head CE; next distill Stage933 row-level policy targets or initialize from accepted specialist heads.

Distillation improves exception relative to Stage935 but still calibrates relation to alpha 0 and loses composition/relation gains.
